## Historical audit — S0281

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/test/bw_0023/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only chunk 2 of 2 is visible; the referenced images themselves are not available for independent inspection.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal and initial work — line 21, `model_request`, chars [0,147568) | The task was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph as editable 3D geometry with matching camera and framing. The student interpreted it as a Gothic hall with vaults, columns, stairs, railing, chandelier and two spheres. This is the student’s semantic inventory, not independent confirmation of the reference. |
| Multiple objects and connections — lines 23–24, `model_response` and `execute`, chars [0,14013) and [0,13747) | The final program defines separate named assets and child primitives for architecture, stair treads and railing, chandelier parts and two spheres. Rod endpoints and common stair coordinates express intended connections; naming and code alone do not verify that parts visually meet or occupy the correct image positions. No articulated character pose is evidenced; the relevant orientation change is the stair assembly’s −38° rotation. |
| Materials, camera and light — lines 21 and 24 | The code specifies procedural noise and bump for stone, a view-dependent colored bubble shader, magenta and emissive materials, a camera and three area lights. The student changed lighting and bubble size/position while retaining the camera. Material assignment depends on realized object lineage; actual appearance and framing cannot be checked from text alone. The program also sets render engine and resolution despite instructions not to change runner rendering settings; the effective runner settings are not established here. |
| Autonomous revision — lines 21, 23–24 | After step 1, the student reported pale architecture, a small bubble, frontal stairs, a dim far opening and a ceiling seam, and revised the scene. After step 2, it reported a frontal stair, centered tunnel and fully visible bubble; it rotated the stairs, moved and enlarged the bubble, and changed lighting. These are student diagnoses and executed code changes, not independent visual findings. |
| Validation and outcome — line 21; lines 26, 28–30, chars [0,1607), [0,1596), [0,49247), [0,59) | Steps 1 and 2 reported successful builds and renders. Step 3 also built and rendered with return code 0, `ok: true`, and was selected. This is **technical execution success**, not verified reconstruction accuracy. No post-step-3 visual comparison or formal quality verdict is visible. |
| Teacher input — lines 21–30 | No distinct teacher diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is visible in this chunk. The system’s general reconstruction instructions and the runner’s render-and-compare prompts are observed inputs, not evidence of a separate teacher intervention. |

**Transferable lesson:** iterative render feedback can motivate localized, editable revisions, but successful execution and hierarchy do not establish visual or geometric correctness. **Task-specific hypotheses:** rotating this stair and shifting this bubble might improve the particular composition; the final image, part contacts, textures, illumination and camera match remain unverified. Earlier unseen history and any later evaluation remain unknown.
